text:
marie-cs: FYI Acme just escalated — they say audit log entries for several critical keystore ops are missing since last night's KMS/HSM patch. customer angry and asking for proof for their compliance audit.
henry-oncall: copying logs now, can you share exact timestamps or sample request IDs from Acme?
marie-cs: they sent 3 request IDs: req_8a3f, req_8a4b, req_8a6c. They say calls returned 200 but no audit row. timeline: patch deployed at 02:13 UTC.
henry-oncall: looking at host-side logs. initial grep: 
```
2026-03-16T02:13:45Z INFO keystore.unwrap req=req_8a3f status=200 kms_key=kek-01 audit_id=
2026-03-16T02:14:12Z INFO keystore.unwrap req=req_8a4b status=200 kms_key=kek-01 audit_id=
2026-03-16T02:15:02Z INFO keystore.unwrap req=req_8a6c status=200 kms_key=kek-01 audit_id=
```
henry-oncall: audit_id empty in those lines — seems the audit indexing step didn't attach IDs.
maya-security: this correlates with CVE-2026-0421 (we rolled our patched HSM agent last night). Patch combined an indexing change and a deferred flush, possible race. Security already flagged a risky path.
chris-engruntime: confirmed: the indexing worker defers zero-length payloads after decrypt if metadata absent. I see a PR that changed the flush window (PR #4123).
olivia-account: Acme is asking for ETA to get full audit export and a compliance statement. They need bridging evidence within 24h.
henry-oncall: short-term mitigation: re-run audit indexer for the affected time window and reconcile missing rows, then provide export. I'm starting a job: `scripts/reindex-audit --start 2026-03-16T02:00 --end 2026-03-16T03:00 --filter kek-01`
marie-cs: please include how many rows expected and what we can certify. They want whether any plaintext key material left on disk.
sre-lead: we should also snapshot the HSM logs and lock the instance to prevent further writes until reindex completes.
chris-engruntime: reindex dry-run shows ~142 audit events with empty audit_id in that window on node hsm-12. I'll kick the reindex now.
deploy-bot: Reindex job started by henry-oncall: job-id rj-20260316-01.
henry-oncall: reindex completed: 142 rows reattached, 0 rows with suspicious payloads. checksum matches expected message digests. Exporting CSV now.
maya-security: good — two asks from security side: 1) we need to produce a forensics note describing root cause (race in flush vs indexing) and list of affected model keys, 2) decide if we need to roll back or hotfix for customers still patching.
chris-engruntime: patch fix: revert PR #4123's deferred-flush logic; hotfix branch ready (hotfix/hsm-index-fix). Will schedule canary deploy to 1 region then global if green.
olivia-account: Acme wants a timeline — can we give them ETA? They asked for a formal note to satisfy auditors.
henry-oncall: ETA: reindex/export done (I attached CSV to case), forensics note draft in 2 hours, hotfix can be canaried in 4 hours and full rollout in 8 hours pending canary health.
maya-security: classify urgency as P0 for affected customers under audit. Prepare CVE advisory wording: reference CVE-2026-0421, impact = missing audit metadata on keystore unwraps, exploitation = low (race condition during indexing), mitigation = reindex + hotfix, timeline + contact.
marie-cs: forwarding export and initial forensics summary to Acme, mentioning patch ETA. Will keep them updated.
chris-engruntime: quick repro steps (internal) for engineering: 
1) run `make test-hsm` with `HSM_AGENT_FLUSH_WINDOW=0`
2) simulate keystore.unwrap concurrent ops (~200 rps)
3) observe indexer logs: `indexer DEBUG dropped empty-audit-metadata`
4) run `scripts/reindex-audit --fix-empty` to repair
henry-oncall: note for SRE: we should add an alert for audit_id-empty > 10/min post-deploy.
sre-lead: created alert `audit.index.missing_ids` (severity=high).
deploy-bot: Hotfix branch created: hotfix/hsm-index-fix by chris-engruntime. Canary scheduled at 06:30 UTC.
maya-security: advise legal/compliance to prepare customer advisory draft. I'll review technical language.
olivia-account: I'll send Acme the CSV, the forensics stub, and the hotfix ETA (canary 4h, full 8h). They'll ask for statement to their auditor — keep me posted on final wording.
marie-cs: Acme replied: "Thanks, we need a signed statement if possible — can security/legal do that?"
maya-security: yes we can prepare signed PSR after final root cause.
chris-engruntime: post-mortem actions: revert deferred flush change, add unit tests around indexer, add canary monitor, add backfill tooling to cli.
henry-oncall: closing loop: export uploaded to case file, hotfix in flight, security drafting advisory. If anyone sees additional missing IDs outside that window, ping me immediately. :thumbsup:
marie-cs: thanks all — I'll update Acme and close the escalation once they confirm auditors satisfied.
